designDecisions.decision: The base is the LONGEST known base district that prefixes the published value at a separator boundary.
designDecisions.why: CS and CS-1 are BOTH rows in austin-tx.json and BOTH exact-match the router's normalizeCode. A first-token split of CS-1-MU-V-NCCD-ETOD-DBETOD-NP yields CS, which resolves, matches and stamps the wrong district's setbacks silently (matched, 0.9 confidence). Truncation here is not a conservative miss.

designDecisions.decision: The vocabulary is Austin's own setback `district_name` leading tokens, listed explicitly in zoning-layers.ts (AUSTIN_BASE_CODES, 37 entries) and asserted EQUAL to the table's leading-token set by a test that reads the table at source.
designDecisions.why: A base this parser returns must normalize to a code the router exact-matches, or the parse has not helped. cad-ingest does not import adapters, so an explicit list plus a binding test beats an implicit read (a typo in a table row would otherwise become the parser's vocabulary silently).
designDecisions.verified: 37/37: every member normalizes to itself and every table leading token is present (test 'equals austin-tx.json's district-code set exactly')

designDecisions.decision: '.' and '&' are NOT separators. Only -, /, and whitespace start a token.
designDecisions.why: R&D is one district and San Marcos publishes SF-4.5; treating '.' or '&' as a boundary could match SF-4 inside SF-4.5 — the exact truncation this design exists to prevent.
designDecisions.tested: 'SF-4.5' with only SF-4 in the vocabulary returns unrecognised (never SF-4)

designDecisions.decision: When no known base prefixes the value: kind 'unrecognised', base null, and the stamp writes the PUBLISHED VALUE verbatim.
designDecisions.why: The published value is a fact about the parcel, and the router has a designed decline path for a code it cannot resolve (mapDistrict -> null -> a named reason). Writing NULL would assert 'no zoning on record', which is false, and writing a shorter token is the wrong district. The parcel is still counted apart in parcelsUnrecognised + unrecognisedHistogram so the gap is a worklist, not a silence.
designDecisions.changedMidLane: This was first implemented as NULL-on-unrecognised and changed after finding the router's decline path; the change is in the diff, and CP1 is where it is disclosed.

designDecisions.decision: Planned-development (PUD/PDD/PD/PC) is its own bucket, stamped RAW so A-164's PUD message still fires.
designDecisions.why: PUD parcels cannot be given a district row; they are not a parse failure and not an acquisition gap. The pattern text and flag are copied VERBATIM from P-255's census so the stamp and the census mean the same thing by the words.

designDecisions.decision: The parser checks the vocabulary FIRST, so a city that really rows a PD/PC/PUD district resolves it as a district; the census (raw code only) would call it planned development.
designDecisions.why: One stated divergence, measured empty for Austin: no AUSTIN_BASE_CODES entry is PD-shaped, and the test asserts parser-kind vs census-regex agreement over all 557 live values.

designDecisions.decision: Every stamped parcel lands in exactly ONE of four buckets, and the four are reported so they can be summed: parcelsMatched, parcelsPlannedDevelopment, parcelsUnrecognised, parcelsUnmatched.
designDecisions.why: 'outside the city' and 'in a district this vocabulary does not carry' are different facts and only the second is work owed.
designDecisions.invariant: the CLI prints the sum next to parcelsRead and calls the equality out; the dry run is where it is checked on real data

designDecisions.decision: overlayHistogram counts overlays ONLY for parcels whose base district resolved.
designDecisions.why: For a resolved base the parser can PROVE which tokens are the base and which are the suffix. Counting a planned-development or unrecognised value's tokens would report the district inside I-SF-2, and PUD inside PUD-NP, as 'overlay tokens' — an invented classification. They are omitted, not guessed.
designDecisions.caughtBy: the CP1 self-review (the first implementation counted them; see adversarialReviewFindings)

designDecisions.decision: The classifier is a pure function with the rule swappable (matchMode: longest-match | shortest-match | first-token), and only the registry is ever configured.
designDecisions.why: Falsifier 4 has to run THIS parser with the rule removed, not a paraphrase of it. A test asserts no registry entry ever ships a non-default matchMode.

adversarialReviewFindings.finding: A structural defect in the four-bucket rewrite: the unrecognised branch had been written as the plain `else`, so the base/planned-development branch was unreachable and every hit would have been reported as unrecognised.
adversarialReviewFindings.howCaught: tsc, on the first typecheck of the change set (TS1128 in zoning-stamp-db.ts). No test would have caught it: the unit tests exercise the pure functions, and the bucket routing lives in the DB-blocked path.
adversarialReviewFindings.lesson: The bucket-routing code is now covered by a test at the layer boundary (reduceZoningFeature + buildZoningIndex + layerParseAudit) so the branch condition itself is exercised without a database.

adversarialReviewFindings.finding: An overlay-histogram miscount (see designDecisions): planned-development and unrecognised tokens were being bumped as overlays.
adversarialReviewFindings.howCaught: writing the CP1 numbers by hand and noticing 'SF' and 'PUD' would appear as overlay tokens

adversarialReviewFindings.finding: A doc comment contradicted the shipped behaviour: zoningCodeAtPoint said an unresolved value 'must never be written to a parcel' while the stamp writes it verbatim (deliberately).
adversarialReviewFindings.howCaught: re-reading the diff against the decision; the comment was corrected

adversarialReviewFindings.finding: SF-4 is a real published Austin base district (5 polygons, 1 distinct value) that austin-tx.json does NOT row (it rows SF-4A, SF-4B, SF-5, SF-6). It is therefore stamped verbatim and counted unrecognised.
adversarialReviewFindings.whyItMatters: It is the live proof of the 'never cut a suffix to reach a row' rule, and it is also a TABLE gap for P-258's owners, not a parser gap. Reported, not silently rounded into SF-4A.

adversarialReviewFindings.finding: The dispatch's premise 'ZONING_BASE collapses codes (SF and MF with no numeric suffix)' is confirmed at source, and one detail is worth recording: the layer's 558-row vocabulary contains NO value starting with PD/PDD/PC, and the only PD-shaped values are the 5 PUD* ones.
adversarialReviewFindings.whyItMatters: it makes the census-vs-parser PD comparison exact rather than approximate

adversarialReviewFindings.finding: The live layer publishes a value with an embedded space ('LR -NP', 1 polygon). 'LR' + overlay 'NP' is the only reading consistent with the layer's other 556 values.
adversarialReviewFindings.howCaught: the whole-vocabulary parse test (the whitespace token rule)

This lane therefore compares AGGREGATES and CODE SETS, states which store each number came from, and does NOT present a per-parcel delta it cannot compute. A per-parcel join (P-255's census re-run after the stamp is applied) is the close's status condition, not this dry run's output.
